# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 36 (Bi-Vb Pc36)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc36  
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 36  
**Title (English, from literature):** Socializing with a householder  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Saṁsaṭṭha Sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 36) is a rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka prohibiting a Buddhist nun from living in ongoing or inappropriate socialization with a householder or a householder's son (*saṁsaṭṭhā vihareyya gahapatinā vā gahapatiputtena vā*) [Hüsken 1997; Wijayaratna 1990; Collett 2014]. According to the origin story, the rule was promulgated when the nun Caṇḍakālī maintained an overly intimate relationship with a lay householder and his son [Collett 2014]. If a nun persistently engages in such inappropriate association despite being reproved, she must confess a *pācittiya* offense.

Scholars have drawn attention to the unusual formal procedure encoded in this rule: Ute Hüsken observes that Pācittiya 36 is the only rule for nuns outside the *saṅghādisesa* class that prescribes a formal threefold admonition (*samanubhāsanā*), a procedural requirement otherwise alien to the *pācittiya* category [Hüsken 1997].

 The rule has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
